name: BSF Capital
legal_name: Saudi Fransi Capital (a Saudi closed joint stock company), trading as 'BSF Capital'
founded: BSF AR 2025 milestones give 2008 ('Launch of BSF Capital (investment arm)'). BSF Capital's press boilerplate (Feb 2025) says 'established in 1985' (seen in search results only). CMA licence 11153-37 per Saudi Exchange fund filings (seen in search results only).
ownership_summary: Wholly owned by Banque Saudi Fransi (100%). Capital SAR 1,000 million per BSF's 2025 Board report; the AR's BSF Capital section says it was incorporated with paid-up capital of SAR 500 million.
government_link: Indirect only through the parent; BSF has no government entity among its 5%+ shareholders (see sa-bsf).
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of BSF (sa-bsf), fully consolidated. Its results drive BSF's 'Investment banking and brokerage' segment. FY2025 BSF Capital net income before zakat SAR 399.0m (6.7% of group) and total income SAR 710.3m. BSF provided an overdraft facility of SAR 1,330m at 31 Dec 2025. Double counting: AUM and segment figures appear in both files; never add them to sa-bsf. Sister wealth entity: Sur Multi Family Office Limited (UK) is owned directly by the bank, not by BSF Capital.
footprint: Saudi Arabia. Headquartered in Riyadh with 'multiple locations across Saudi Arabia'; FY2025 income reported for Western, Eastern and Central regions plus head office. International brokerage access for clients.
customer_segments: Local and international financial institutions, corporates, government entities and individual investors (AR 2025), including BSF private banking and affluent clients.
business_lines: Investment banking (ECM, DCM, M&A, underwriting; 2025 deals include the Flynas, Sport Clubs and Almajdiah IPOs and the ACWA Power rights issue), asset management (public and private funds, real estate funds, discretionary portfolios), wealth management and investment advisory, debt and equity research, institutional sales and trading, local and international brokerage, custody.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Saudi Fransi Capital, branded BSF Capital since the June 2024 group rebrand, is BSF's 100% CMA-licensed investment arm. It covers investment banking, asset management, research, institutional sales and trading, local and international brokerage, and custody. AUM was SAR 34.8bn at 30 Jun 2026 (SAR 31.0bn at end-2025), and the firm employed 229 people at end-2025. In 2025 it repositioned wealth management from product-driven to advisory-led, aiming to be 'the wealth advisor of choice in the Kingdom'. It also expanded its BlackRock partnership (Feb 2025) to give clients globally diversified, Shariah-compliant multi-asset portfolios, and began building a digital wealth platform whose first output, the 'BSF Invest App', was scheduled for early 2026. Under the parent's Strategy 2030 the arm's priorities are 'Wealth management acceleration' and a 'brokerage system upgrade'. The strategy was refreshed around institutional and private banking clients in mid-2026, after a CEO change (Apr 2026) and a wealth-head change (May 2026). Brokerage and asset management fees fell 22% YoY in Q1 2026 and 17% in H1 2026.

private_banking.detail: Private banking sits in the parent's Personal Banking Group (see sa-bsf). BSF Capital provides investment advisory, asset management and brokerage to BSF Private Banking clients, and its 2026 strategy refresh focuses on institutional and private banking clients.

asset_management.detail: AUM SAR 34.8bn (30 Jun 2026). Mutual funds (conventional and Shariah-compliant, KSA and international markets), open-ended and publicly traded funds, private placements and discretionary portfolios (parent PB page). Islamic mutual funds SAR 3,303m at end-2025. 2025 launches: eight real estate funds (mixed use, hospitality, industrial, residential; expected development value above SAR 5bn), a fund for the Kingdom's first all-inclusive Rixos resort, a film investment fund and an industrial-city fund in Riyadh. Award: Best Performance Investment Fund (Sukuk and International Bonds category), Sanadeq Media Group.

brokerage.detail: Local and international securities brokerage, custody, margin lending, institutional sales and trading, and research. Brokerage trading value SAR 17.8bn in 2Q 2026 and SAR 13.9bn in 1Q 2026. Q1 2026 call: 'upgrading our brokerage platform'. Strategy 2030: 'Upgrade brokerage ecosystem'.

digital_investing.detail: An existing brokerage platform is being upgraded (Q1 2026 call). The current app name was not confirmed from an official page; a mobile trading app called 'Fransi Tadawul' appeared in search results only. AR 2025: BSF Capital began implementing a digital wealth platform whose first output is the 'BSF Invest App', planned for early 2026. It was to be mobile-first, give access to globally diversified portfolios, and later add BSF Capital mutual and private funds. No launch announcement or app-store listing was found by 12 Oct 2026.

advisory.detail: Holds a CMA licence for advising (AR 2025). Investment advisory is offered to BSF Private Banking clients. In 2025 it built a specialist internal investment-solutions team and moved to an advisory-led, data-driven client engagement model. Saudi Exchange fund filings describe the CMA licence (11153-37) as covering dealing, arranging, managing, advising and custody (search result only).

discretionary.detail: Discretionary portfolio management is listed among BSF Capital asset management services (parent PB page). Discretionary AUM is not disclosed.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Through BlackRock, clients 'now have access to investment portfolios which are globally diversified and sharia compliant' (AR 2025), delivered through advisory. The planned BSF Invest App would offer diversified portfolios digitally. No live robo service was confirmed.

funds_platform.detail: Own funds plus third-party funds: parent PB page cites relationships with BlackRock, Nomura and Ashmore for funds and private placements. No fund-platform technology vendor named.

structured_products.detail: No structured products found at BSF Capital level in sources read (the parent bank offers structured deposits; see sa-bsf). Own website not accessible.

private_markets.detail: Private placements and real estate / hospitality / film / industrial development funds launched in 2025 (see asset_management).
